candidates.label: Chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) exacerbated by olaparib
missing_or_uncertain: Response to steroids or IVIG not documented

candidates.label: Thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) secondary to olaparib or malignancy
missing_or_uncertain: LDH, haptoglobin, ADAMTS13 activity not available

candidates.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) due to metastatic prostate cancer
Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) or bone marrow failure from prior therapy
missing_or_uncertain: Peripheral smear and bone marrow biopsy not performed

response.rationale: The temporal relationship between olaparib initiation and purpura/thrombocytopenia strongly supports drug-induced myelosuppression (D1). The prior low platelet count (F10) suggests a possible chronic ITP (D2), but the acute onset after olaparib makes D1 more likely. TMA (D3) and DIC (D4) are considered but lack supporting laboratory evidence. MDS (D5) is less likely given the acute onset and lack of prior cytotoxic therapy. The margin is medium because the history of low platelets 5 years earlier introduces uncertainty.
